subject: Request: Authorization for Temporary Latency Deviation & Credit Cap (ArborTech renewal)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia@arbortech.com>
Cc: ArborTech Legal <contracts@arbortech.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal ask — temporary latency tolerance + cap on service credits (RDW-2026-3483)

Priya / Marissa — quick summary: ArborTech is set to renew on 10/25 for their enterprise plan (deal RDW-2026-3483). They want a three-month, temporary adjustment to our latency SLA to accommodate a major marketing campaign that will spike inference traffic. Their ask: lower guaranteed tail latency commitment (effectively tolerate higher 95th/99th p99 latency) and limit any service credit exposure in that window to a fixed cap (they suggested 12% of monthly invoice).

Why now: client is committing to +40% committed spend if we accept the temporary term. They are sensitive to switching costs and have given an internal timeline — if we can’t provide concessions they will push the renewal to another vendor.

Attached: arbortech_mau_report.csv (traffic profile), preliminary PO and expected committed spend.

Asking for: executive confirmation for a non-standard SLA term (3 months) and approval for a service-credit cap. Can you weigh in on acceptable cap and any required guardrails (e.g., burst capacity purchase, limited to hosted region us-west)? We need yes/no and any conditions in the next 48 hours to hit their renewal date.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal ask — temporary latency tolerance + cap on service credits (RDW-2026-3483)

Marissa / Jonas — tagging you both for deal-desk + finance input. Ben flagged this as time-sensitive. A few thoughts before we take to execs/legal: 

- Need clear definition: do they want an uptime change (e.g., 99.9 -> 99.5) or a relaxed latency target (p99 tail increase)? Those have different remediation calculus.
- Proposed mitigation: require ArborTech to purchase a 3-month burst block (Dedicated reservation) and prepay it. That lowers our exposure while giving them extra headroom for the campaign.
- If we do an SLA amendment, I recommend capping credits at a percentage of committed monthly spend — but lower than their 12% ask. Suggest a cap in the 7–10% range with the following conditions: limited to Oct–Dec 2026, applies only to hosted region us-west, and requires executed amendment before campaign start.

Jonas — can you run exposure numbers for 8% vs 12% cap and confirm the P&L impact? Marissa — if this approach is acceptable, we need deal-desk exec approval + legal to draft a redline quickly.

Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Renewal ask — temporary latency tolerance + cap on service credits (RDW-2026-3483)

Priya / Marissa — numbers below (ran against current usage + projected campaign uplift):

- Baseline monthly committed spend: $180,000
- Projected campaign uplift: +40% => $252,000 (if they follow through)
- If we accept a 12% credit cap, worst-case credit exposure (single month) = $30,240
- If we accept an 8% cap, worst-case = $20,160
- Recommended approach reduces downside by ~33% (8% vs 12%) while still being meaningful to the customer.

Additional points:
- Require prepayment for burst capacity (3-month term) — incremental revenue of ~$22k one-time; lowers latency events materially.
- Operational burden: our SREs estimate one additional on-call rotation to monitor campaign window if we sign — minor but note it.

I've uploaded a short one-page deal summary (deal_summary.pdf) to the deal link in the metadata. From a finance POV, 8% cap + prepay looks acceptable if marketing/legal sign off.

Jonas
Director, Commercial Finance
jonas.weber@redwood.com

On Wed, Oct 21, 2026 at 11:03 AM Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ArborTech Legal <contracts@arbortech.com>
Date: 2026-10-23T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Approval: Conditional exception granted for ArborTech renewal (RDW-2026-3483)

Team / Olivia — after reviewing the business case and finance impact, I am authorizing a limited, conditional exception for ArborTech. Terms approved: 

1) Temporary latency deviation: effective 2026-10-25 through 2026-12-31. We will accept an operational tolerance that de-rates p99 tail targets in region us-west for that window (documented in the amendment). This is a time-boxed operational concession, not a permanent SLA change.

2) Service credit cap: capped at 8% of the monthly committed spend for any month during the concession window. This is a hard cap and the remedy is limited to service credit only (no additional refunds or fee waivers beyond the credit calculation).

3) Commercial guardrails: ArborTech must purchase a 3-month burst reservation and prepay it before the amendment becomes effective. If they do not prepay, the temporary deviation is void.

4) Documentation & timing: Legal to prepare a short amendment (redline requested). Signatures from both parties required prior to Oct 25. If the amendment is not fully executed by the campaign start, we revert to standard SLA terms and no credits are owed.

5) Measurement: SRE will instrument hourly monitoring for the campaign window and provide a post-campaign runbook with incidents/metrics. Any credit calculation will use the same telemetry we use for standard SLA calculations.

Ben — please convey the conditions to Olivia and ArborTech legal. Once they confirm acceptance, loop Legal (contracts@redwood.com) to finalize the redline and then send the DocuSign link.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

- Service credit cap: 8% of monthly committed spend (applies to any month in the window).
